The sticky behavior on the align axis. `partial` will keep the content in the boundary as long as the anchor is at
least partially in the boundary whilst "always" will keep the content in the boundary regardless.

members.align: The preferred alignment against the anchor. May change when collisions occur.
members.alignflip:
Flip alignment when colliding with boundary.
May only occur when `prioritizePosition` is true.
members.alignoffset: An offset in pixels from the `start` or `end` alignment options.
members.arrowpadding:
The padding between the arrow and the edges of the content. If your content has border-radius, this will prevent it
from overflowing the corners.
members.avoidcollisions: When `true`, overrides the side and align preferences to prevent collisions with boundary edges.
members.collisionboundary:
The element used as the collision boundary. By default this is the viewport, though you can provide additional
element(s) to be included in this check.
members.collisionpadding:
The distance in pixels from the boundary edges where collision detection should occur. Accepts a number (same for
all sides), or a partial padding object, for example: { top: 20, left: 20 }.
members.disableoutsidepointerevents:
When `true`, hover/focus/click interactions will be disabled on elements outside the `DismissableLayer`. Users will
need to click twice on outside elements to interact with them: once to close the `DismissableLayer`, and again to
trigger the element.
members.disableupdateonlayoutshift: Whether to disable the update position for the content when the layout shifted.
members.forcemount:
Used to force mounting when more control is needed.

Useful when controlling animation with Vue animation libraries.
members.hideshiftedarrow:
When `true`, hides the arrow when it cannot be centered
to the reference element.
members.hidewhendetached: Whether to hide the content when the anchor becomes fully occluded.
members.open:
Whether the floating layer is open. Drives the positioning lifecycle (`isPositioned`
resets when open flips); the positioning primitive itself has no open state, so
consumers wire their own open state here.
members.placement:
The placement of the floating element.

If used, it will override the `side` and `align` props.
members.popupprops: Properties forwarded to the popup element.
members.positionstrategy: The type of CSS position property to use.
members.prioritizeposition: Force content to be position within the viewport. Might overlap the reference element, which may not be desired.
members.reference:
The custom element or virtual element that will be set as the reference to position the floating element. If
provided, it will replace the default anchor element.
members.side:
The preferred side of the anchor to render against when open. Will be reversed when collisions occur and
avoidCollisions is enabled.
members.sideflip: Flip to the opposite side when colliding with boundary.
members.sideoffset: The distance in pixels from the anchor.
members.sticky:
The sticky behavior on the align axis. `partial` will keep the content in the boundary as long as the anchor is at
least partially in the boundary whilst "always" will keep the content in the boundary regardless.
members.trapfocus: When `true`, focus cannot escape the content via keyboard, pointer, or a programmatic focus.
members.updatepositionstrategy: Strategy to update the position of the floating element on every animation frame.

The padding between the arrow and the edges of the content. If your content has border-radius, this will prevent it
from overflowing the corners.
members.avoidcollisions: When `true`, overrides the side and align preferences to prevent collisions with boundary edges.
members.collisionboundary:
The element used as the collision boundary. By default this is the viewport, though you can provide additional
element(s) to be included in this check.
members.collisionpadding:
The distance in pixels from the boundary edges where collision detection should occur. Accepts a number (same for
all sides), or a partial padding object, for example: { top: 20, left: 20 }.

When `true`, hovering the popup closes instead of keeping it open (the grace area is disabled,
so leaving the trigger closes the layer immediately).

members.forcemount:

Useful when controlling animation with Vue animation libraries.
members.hideshiftedarrow:
When `true`, hides the arrow when it cannot be centered
to the reference element.
members.hidewhendetached: Whether to hide the content when the trigger becomes fully occluded.

members.placement:

members.popupprops: Properties forwarded to the popup element.
members.positionstrategy: The type of CSS position property to use.
members.prioritizeposition: Force content to be position within the viewport. Might overlap the reference element, which may not be desired.
members.reference:

members.sideflip: Flip to the opposite side when colliding with boundary.
members.sideoffset: The distance in pixels from the trigger.
members.sticky:

least partially in the boundary whilst "always" will keep the content in the boundary regardless.
members.trapfocus:
Whether focus is trapped inside the popup while open (Tab cycles within the layer and body
scroll is locked for modal layers).

members.expandstrategy:
The expand strategy of the nested vertical TreeMenu pane.

- `keep`: keep the current expanded state; manually expanded or collapsed menus are not affected by activating other menus. The collapsible ancestors of the selected menu are expanded on mount and whenever the selected menu changes from outside (e.g. driven by an external route), so it stays visible.
- `selected`: only expand the currently selected menu and all its ancestor menus; non-selected menus are collapsed when the selected menu changes.

Only applies to the nested `TreeMenuCompact`; the nested horizontal pane
(`TreeNavCompact`) has no expand strategy.

members.modelvalue:
The selected leaf value of the SplitNav component. Can be bound with `v-model`.

Parent items are not written here; clicking them only opens the nested pane.
members.verticalmountedid:
The id of the element to mount vertical menus into (rendered via `Teleport`).

callables.top_left:
Custom content rendered above the first-level rail of a dual-vertical menu.

The cell is as wide as the rail, so a brand can sit in the menu's own
top-left corner instead of beside it; the divider between the two columns is
the pane's own leading edge, so it runs through this band as well.
`collapsed` reports whether the nested pane is folded.
callables.top_right:
Custom content rendered above the nested pane of a dual-vertical menu.

The cell only renders while the pane column exists — the active first-level
item has visible children — and follows that column's width, folded state
included. `collapsed` reports whether the pane is folded.

packages_ui_src_components_app_shell_typ.appshellmode:
Shell skeleton of the `SAppShell` component.

The four `SplitNavMode` literals are forwarded to `SSplitNav` unchanged — the
shell only decides where each pane is mounted. `sidebar` and `top` are the
single-pane shells (one nested `STreeMenu`, or one horizontal `STreeNav`).

Mode names describe the **menu shape**, not the layout orientation. The
layout orientation is derived from the mode: a vertical first level makes the
sidebar span the full height (`orientation="horizontal"`), a horizontal first
level puts the header across the top (`orientation="vertical"`).

The mode describes the **desktop** shape. In the mobile view the shell renders
the `sidebar` skeleton for every mode — the sidebar is the layout's drawer
there, and a drawer holds one nested tree — while this prop keeps reporting
what the host bound. See the AppShell docs, "Mobile view".

members.breadcrumbs:
Breadcrumb items rendered in the header.

Omit it to derive the breadcrumb from `items` and the active value: the
trail from the root menu down to the active item, where every ancestor
whose menu has children opens a dropdown of those children — nested like
the menu itself, so an entry that has children keeps its own submenu.
Provide it to render a plain breadcrumb from your own data instead.
members.breadcrumbvisible:
Whether the breadcrumb region renders when the trail is not empty.

The region is hidden below the `md` breakpoint either way: a phone header
keeps its trigger and its trailing actions. Bind `ui.breadcrumb` (e.g.
`lt-md:flex`) to bring it back there.
members.class: Additional class names applied to the shell root element.
members.defaultmobileopen: The open state of the mobile drawer when it is initially rendered.
members.defaultopen: The expanded state of the sidebar when initially rendered.
members.expandstrategy:
The expand strategy of the rendered menu.

- `keep`: keep the current expanded state; manually expanded or collapsed menus are not affected by activating other menus. The collapsible ancestors of the selected menu are expanded on mount and whenever the selected menu changes from outside (e.g. driven by an external route), so it stays visible.
- `selected`: only expand the currently selected menu and all its ancestor menus; non-selected menus are collapsed when the selected menu changes.

The shell defaults to `selected`: the navigation mirrors the current route,
so one path stays expanded and the active entry keeps its place instead of
competing with the branches opened earlier in the session.

Applies to the single `STreeMenu` (`sidebar` mode) and to the nested vertical
panes of `SSplitNav` (the split modes). `top` mode renders `STreeNav`, which
has no expand strategy. `menuProps.tree` / `menuProps.split` take precedence
over this prop.
members.ismobile:
Whether the shell is in mobile view.

When omitted, it is forwarded unset and `SLayout` resolves the mode: a
viewport published by a host through `provideViewportContext`, then
`useMediaQuery('(max-width: 767.9px)')`. Pass an explicit boolean to force
it, e.g. for a server-side detection.

members.layoutprops:
Properties forwarded to `SLayout`.

Shell-owned options (`open`, `orientation`, `sidebarVisible`, `isMobile`,
`pxToRem`) are derived from `mode`; `sidebarWidth` and
`collapsedSidebarWidth` default to the widths the mode requires — override
them only when the menu panes do not need to line up.

Per-slot class overrides for the internal `SLayout`. Takes precedence over
the shell's `layout*` UI slots.
members.logoplacement:
Placement of the brand region.

`auto` follows the skeleton the shell renders; `sidebar` and `sidebar-bottom`
need a skeleton whose sidebar is always a column of its own — see
`AppShellLogoPlacement` for the modes that support the bottom placement. In
the mobile view that skeleton is the `sidebar` one, so `auto` puts the brand
in the drawer whatever mode is bound.

The shell renders the drawer through `SLayout`, where the drawer is the

The **desktop** skeleton: in the mobile view the shell renders the `sidebar`

members.customtoast: Whether to use custom toast rendering. If set to `true`, the `ToastProvider` will not render the default toast UI, and you can import `ToastProvider` component to render custom toast UI.
members.dir:
The global reading direction of your application. This will be inherited by all components.

When omitted, the direction follows the current locale and falls back to `'ltr'`.
members.iconrender: A function to render the icon. This is useful when you want to use a custom icon library or want to wrap the icon with a custom component.
members.isserver:
Whether the component is running in a server environment.

The UI library is pre-built, so `import.meta.env.SSR` is baked at build
time and cannot detect the consumer's runtime. This defaults to runtime
detection (`typeof window === 'undefined'`), and can be overridden with
the app's own flag (e.g. Nuxt's `import.meta.server`) when the app is
bundled for both server and client.
members.linkcomponent:
The component used by `Link` to render internal links. This is useful when you want to
integrate a framework-specific link component (e.g. Nuxt `NuxtLink`, a custom `RouterLink`
wrapper, or a locale-prefixing `Link`) instead of the globally registered `RouterLink`.

When omitted, `Link` resolves the global `RouterLink` and falls back to a native `<a>`.
members.locale: The global locale of your application. This will be inherited by all components.
members.messages:
Overrides for built-in component locale messages. Merged on top of the locale selected by the
`locale` prop, so you only need to supply the keys you want to change.
members.nonce: The global `nonce` value of your application. This will be inherited by the related components.
members.persisttheme:
Whether to enable persisted theme reading from localStorage.

When disabled (default), the ConfigProvider only consumes the explicit
`theme` prop and never reads or writes any storage, keeping the current
behavior. When enabled, the persisted theme envelope fills in keys not
explicitly provided by `theme`, and changes are written back through a
single debounced writer.
members.presetprovider:
The server-side custom theme preset registry resolver.

Maps a stored preset name to its definition so SSR can render custom
presets without localStorage access. Only used when `persistTheme` is
enabled on the server; on the client the presets table (carried by the
theme envelope) is the source of truth.
members.progress: The global top progress configuration of your application.
members.themeconfig:
The persisted theme envelope injected from the server.

Used during SSR to render the same theme the client persisted; on the
client the localStorage envelope is the source of truth.
members.toast: The global toast configuration of your application. This will be inherited by the related components.
members.tooltip: The global tooltip configuration of your application. This will be inherited by the related components.

members.font: font family stacks for sans / heading / mono (runtime-swappable).
members.preset:
A custom color preset: either an inline mode-split override (light/dark
partial tokens) or a `{ name }` reference to a stored preset. Resolved to
`overrides` before the engine resolves the map.
members.primary: the brand palette (any of the 26 built-ins).
members.size: the root font-size preset or length (the density zoom).
members.spacing: the spacing grid unit multiplier (padding / margin / gap / inset).

members.height: The default height of the icon.
members.width: The default width of the icon.

members.ismobile:
Whether the layout is in mobile view.

Resolution order: this prop, then a host viewport decision provided through
`provideViewportContext` (a simulated viewport — a device frame, an embedded
shell), then `useMediaQuery(mobileViewportQuery)` — the same breakpoint the
styled desktop sidebar is hidden at. Pass an explicit boolean to force the
mode (e.g. a server-side detection); `false` re-enables the inline sidebar
even below the breakpoint.

The controlled open state of the mobile drawer. Can be bound with
`v-model:mobileOpen`.

Kept apart from `open`, which drives the desktop sidebar: on mobile the
inline sidebar is replaced by a drawer, so the two states never apply at the
same time.

The expand strategy of the nested vertical TreeMenu pane.

- `keep`: keep the current expanded state; manually expanded or collapsed menus are not affected by activating other menus. The collapsible ancestors of the selected menu are expanded on mount and whenever the selected menu changes from outside (e.g. driven by an external route), so it stays visible.

Properties for the ThemeModeSegment component.

A context-bound segmented control bound to the active `SConfigProvider`
theme. It exposes the three `ThemeModePreference` options — `auto` (follows
the OS `prefers-color-scheme`), `light`, and `dark` — as icon-led segment
options. Visual props are inherited from `SegmentProps` (with `shape`
defaulting to `rounded`); `items`, `modelValue`, and `defaultValue` are not
exposed — the option list is fixed and the state is owned by the theme
context shared across all theme components.

each option.

Properties for the ThemeModeSwitch component.

A context-bound toggle bound to the active `SConfigProvider` theme. It shows
